records.issue_text: mixins.scss:120 declares display: -moz-inline-box, a fabricated property value never implemented by Gecko, misleading readers into thinking Firefox 2009 inline flex is covered
records.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `display: -moz-inline-box;` in `@mixin inline-flex()` (mixins.scss). The finding’s concern is a specific, substantive maintainability/documentation issue: this vendor-prefixed fallback may be misleading if it was never actually supported by Gecko, implying Firefox coverage that doesn’t exist. This is not a functional defect clearly proven by the diff (later `display: inline-flex;` is present), but it is a concrete review concern grounded in the added code.

records.issue_text: header.scss keeps .valign-helper after .contents became a flex container, leaving a dead-but-styled helper that can shift title vertical alignment and is a hazard for future layout edits
records.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` was converted into a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and the old float-based `.title { float: left; }` block was removed. However, the stylesheet still defines `.valign-helper` immediately after, even though a “valign helper” is typically only needed for pre-flex vertical-centering hacks. If the markup still includes a `.valign-helper` element, it will now become an extra flex item and could interfere with alignment/spacing; even if not present, the styled rule is likely dead and a future-layout hazard.

records.issue_text: Flex conversion of .small-action drops avatar/text spacing with no gap replacement, causing avatar and description text to butt against each other
records.rationale: In `.small-action`, the diff converts the container to flex (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) but simultaneously removes the main spacing that previously separated the description from the avatar: `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;`. There is no new `margin-left`/`gap` added between `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`, so the flex children can end up adjacent with minimal separation, matching the finding’s “butt against each other” concern.

records.issue_text: Flex conversion of .small-action removes the 4em left padding, misaligning avatar-less small-action variants flush-left with surrounding posts
records.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action-desc` previously had `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` (explicit 4em left indent) and `margin-top: 5px;`, but the diff changes it to `padding: 0 1.5%;` while also converting `.small-action` to flex (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). This concretely removes the left offset that would keep the description aligned when there isn’t an avatar occupying space, so the described flush-left misalignment mechanism is directly introduced by this change.

records.issue_text: mixins.scss align-items/order mixins pass modern flexbox values verbatim into 2009-spec properties without value translation (e.g. flex-start is invalid for -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align), causing silent layout breakage in legacy browsers
records.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` and `@mixin order($val)` in `mixins.scss` that directly assign the same argument to legacy 2009-era properties (e.g., `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;`, `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val;`). records.issue_text: align-items mixin family is internally inconsistent: -moz-box equivalent for align-items is missing while -moz-box-ordinal-group is included in order()
records.rationale: In mixins.scss the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` sets `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but does not set the `-moz-box-align` equivalent. This is inconsistent with `@mixin flexbox()` which includes `display: -moz-box;` and with `@mixin order($val)` which includes `-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val;`, meaning old `-moz-box` layouts would not get an alignment rule from `align-items`.
records.stripped_text: align-items mixin family is internally inconsistent: -moz-box equivalent for align-items is missing while -moz-box-ordinal-group is included in order()
